data.title: Life as an Edo Samurai
sentences: Before dawn, the samurai’s life began with the meticulous grooming of his topknot and the careful fastening of his two swords.
Though he belonged to the elite class, his role had shifted from battlefield warrior to civil administrator.
His morning was spent managing tax records and grain stores within the lord’s castle walls.
Strict etiquette governed every movement, as any failure to show proper respect could lead to disgrace.
By afternoon, he practiced the dual path of the pen and the sword.
He honed his combat skills in the dojo before turning to Confucian classics or the quiet discipline of meditation.
Despite his high status, many samurai faced economic hardship, sometimes crafting household goods to supplement their fixed rice stipends.
Evenings were reserved for rigid social obligations and the security patrols that kept his district safe.
Guided by the code of Bushido, he lived a life of stoicism, loyalty, and constant preparation.
